probes.query: Where is the helper that computes the longest common prefix between two path strings in the radix tree?
expectedFacts: longestCommonPrefix walks two strings byte-by-byte and returns the index where they first differ
probes.author: go-author
probes.notes: Verified: grep -n 'func longestCommonPrefix' tree.go -> tree.go:61. Body returns i where a[i]!=b[i].

probes.query: Which function picks the request binding implementation based on the HTTP method and Content-Type (e.g. returns the JSON binder for application/json POSTs)?
expectedFacts: binding.Default returns Form for GET, otherwise switches on the content type and returns JSON for MIMEJSON, XML, ProtoBuf, MsgPack, YAML, TOML, etc.
probes.author: go-author
probes.notes: Verified: grep -n 'func Default' binding/binding.go -> binding/binding.go:95. Switches on contentType after a GET->Form short-circuit. Build-tag twin func Default at binding/binding_nomsgpack.go:91 (//go:build nomsgpack) is an accepted-alternative answer (review FIX).

probes.author: go-author
probes.notes: Verified: grep -n 'func BasicAuthForRealm' auth.go -> auth.go:48 (BasicAuth at auth.go:72 delegates to it with empty realm).

probes.query: Where is the 'while(1);' secure-JSON prefix configured on the engine? I want the setter that changes the string prepended to JSON array responses.
expectedFacts: Engine.SecureJsonPrefix assigns its argument to engine.secureJSONPrefix, which Context.SecureJSON later prepends; the render-side SecureJSON type only consumes a Prefix field, it does not configure it
probes.author: go-author
probes.notes: Distractor: surface phrasing ('secure JSON prefix', 'prepended to JSON array responses') lures toward render/json.go SecureJSON.Render (render/json.go:94, type at render/json.go:29) which actually writes the prefix. The CONFIGURED setter the query asks for is gin.go. Verified gold: grep -n 'func (engine \*Engine) SecureJsonPrefix' gin.go -> gin.go:265 (engine.secureJSONPrefix field at gin.go:176, default 'while(1);' at gin.go:224). Wrong target verified present: grep -n 'func (r SecureJSON) Render' render/json.go -> render/json.go:94.

probes.query: Trace how ClientIP decides whether to trust the X-Forwarded-For header — which engine method validates that the direct peer is a trusted proxy and which one parses the forwarded header value?
expectedFacts: Context.ClientIP calls engine.isTrustedProxy on the remote IP and only when trusted (and ForwardedByClientIP is set) iterates RemoteIPHeaders calling engine.validateHeader to extract the client IP
probes.author: go-author
probes.notes: Verified: grep -n 'func (c \*Context) ClientIP' context.go -> context.go:975; grep -n 'func (engine \*Engine) isTrustedProxy' gin.go -> gin.go:469; grep -n 'func (engine \*Engine) validateHeader' gin.go -> gin.go:482. ClientIP body (context.go:1011 calls isTrustedProxy, 1014-1017 loops RemoteIPHeaders + validateHeader).

probes.query: How are Context objects reused across requests instead of being allocated each time, and where are they reset before reuse?
expectedFacts: The Engine keeps a sync.Pool whose New func calls allocateContext; ServeHTTP gets a Context from the pool, calls Context.reset() to clear per-request state, then returns it to the pool after handling
probes.author: go-author
probes.notes: Verified: grep -n 'pool.New' gin.go -> gin.go:229 (engine.pool.New = func()... allocateContext); grep -n 'func (engine \*Engine) allocateContext' gin.go -> gin.go:252; grep -n 'func (c \*Context) reset' context.go -> context.go:103. ServeHTTP uses pool.Get/reset/Put at gin.go:667,670,674.

probes.query: There's a hard cap on how many handlers a route can have in its chain that triggers a 'too many handlers' assertion. Where is the chain merged and what constant bounds its size?
expectedFacts: RouterGroup.combineHandlers asserts the merged handler count is below abortIndex (math.MaxInt8 >> 1 = 63) before copying the group handlers and the route handlers into one chain
probes.author: go-author
probes.notes: Verified: grep -n 'func (group \*RouterGroup) combineHandlers' routergroup.go -> routergroup.go:241; assert1(finalSize < int(abortIndex), "too many handlers") at routergroup.go:243; grep -n 'abortIndex' context.go -> const abortIndex int8 = math.MaxInt8 >> 1 at context.go:57.

probes.query: When a handler panics because the client closed the connection (broken pipe / connection reset), the recovery middleware shouldn't try to write a 500. Where is that broken-pipe case detected and handled differently?
expectedFacts: CustomRecoveryWithWriter sets isBrokenPipe when the recovered error matches syscall.EPIPE, syscall.ECONNRESET, or http.ErrAbortHandler, and in that case records the error and aborts without invoking the normal recovery handler that would write a status
probes.author: go-author
probes.notes: Verified: grep -n 'isBrokenPipe' recovery.go -> recovery.go:63,66,71,81 inside func CustomRecoveryWithWriter (recovery.go:53). errors.Is checks EPIPE/ECONNRESET/http.ErrAbortHandler at recovery.go:66-68; broken-pipe branch calls c.Error(err)+c.Abort() at recovery.go:82-84.

probes.query: When the recovery middleware dumps the failing HTTP request to the log, does it leak the Authorization header? Show me where credentials are scrubbed from the dump.
expectedFacts: secureRequestDump dumps the request and replaces any line beginning with 'Authorization:' with 'Authorization: *' so credentials are not written to the recovery log
probes.author: go-author
probes.notes: Verified: grep -n 'func secureRequestDump' recovery.go -> recovery.go:98; masking at recovery.go:102-103 (strings.HasPrefix(line, "Authorization:") -> lines[i] = "Authorization: *"). Only the Authorization header is sanitized (comment recovery.go:97).

probes.author: go-author
probes.notes: Verified absent: grep -rin 'rate.limit|ratelimit|token.bucket|leaky.bucket|throttle|throttling' --include=*.go . -> 1 result, githubapi_test.go:147 which is only a route literal {http.MethodGet, "/rate_limit"} in a test fixture, NOT a rate-limiter implementation. gin ships no rate-limiting middleware.
